front.en: Name the three arthrokinematic movements.
front.ur: Teen arthrokinematic movements ke naam batayein.

back.en: Roll, glide (slide) and spin.
back.ur: Roll, glide (slide) aur spin.

front.en: Convex surface moving on a fixed concave surface: roll and glide are…?
front.ur: Convex surface, fixed concave surface par move kare: roll aur glide…?

back.en: Opposite directions (e.g. shoulder abduction: humeral head rolls up, glides down).
back.ur: Opposite directions (maslan shoulder abduction: humeral head upar roll, neeche glide).

front.en: Concave surface moving on a fixed convex surface: roll and glide are…?
front.ur: Concave surface, fixed convex surface par move kare: roll aur glide…?

back.en: Same direction (e.g. open-chain knee extension: tibia rolls and glides anterior).
back.ur: Same direction (maslan open-chain knee extension: tibia anterior roll aur anterior glide).

front.en: Rising from a squat (closed chain): which way does the femur glide during knee extension?
front.ur: Squat se uthna (closed chain): knee extension mein femur kis taraf glide karti hai?

back.en: Posterior — the convex femur is moving, so it rolls anterior and glides posterior.
back.ur: Posterior — convex femur move kar rahi hai, is liye anterior roll aur posterior glide.

front.en: Mobilization to gain shoulder abduction, based on the convex–concave rule?
front.ur: Convex–concave rule ke mutabiq shoulder abduction barhane ke liye mobilization?

back.en: Inferior glide of the humerus — then reassess range and pain.
back.ur: Humerus ki inferior glide — phir range aur dard reassess karein.

lessonTitle: Active & Passive Insufficiency — Feel It in Your Own Hand

front.en: Length–tension relationship in one line?
front.ur: Length–tension relationship ek line mein?

back.en: Muscle force is greatest near mid-length; it falls when the muscle is very short or very long.
back.ur: Muscle ki force darmiyani length par zyada; bohat chhota ya bohat lamba ho to kam.

lessonTitle: Active & Passive Insufficiency — Feel It in Your Own Hand

front.en: Define active insufficiency.
front.ur: Active insufficiency ki definition?

back.en: A two-joint muscle is so shortened across both joints that it can't produce effective force or full range at both.
back.ur: Two-joint muscle dono joints par itna chhota ke dono par effective force ya poori range na de sake.

lessonTitle: Active & Passive Insufficiency — Feel It in Your Own Hand

front.en: Define passive insufficiency.
front.ur: Passive insufficiency ki definition?

back.en: A two-joint muscle is so lengthened across both joints that it limits further movement in the opposite direction.
back.ur: Two-joint muscle dono joints par itna lamba ke ulti direction mein mazeed movement rok de.

lessonTitle: Active & Passive Insufficiency — Feel It in Your Own Hand

front.en: Why is a fist weak with the wrist fully flexed?
front.ur: Wrist poori flexed ho to fist weak kyun?

back.en: Active insufficiency of the long finger flexors (plus passive tension in the finger extensors).
back.ur: Lambe finger flexors ki active insufficiency (aur finger extensors ki passive tension).

lessonTitle: Active & Passive Insufficiency — Feel It in Your Own Hand

front.en: How do you tell hamstring tightness from neural tension in an SLR?
front.ur: SLR mein hamstring tightness aur neural tension mein farq kaise?

back.en: Structural differentiation — add ankle dorsiflexion or neck flexion; symptom change suggests a neural contribution.
back.ur: Structural differentiation — ankle dorsiflexion ya neck flexion add karein; symptoms badlein to neural hissa ho sakta hai.

lessonTitle: Muscle Contraction — Concentric, Eccentric, Isometric & Length–Tension

front.en: Define an eccentric contraction.
front.ur: Eccentric contraction ki tareef?

back.en: The muscle lengthens while producing force — it controls (brakes) a movement.
back.ur: Muscle force banate hue lambi hoti hai — movement ko control (brake) karti hai.

lessonTitle: Muscle Contraction — Concentric, Eccentric, Isometric & Length–Tension

front.en: Lowering a dumbbell in a curl: which muscle, which contraction?
front.ur: Curl mein dumbbell neeche lana: kaun si muscle, kaun sa contraction?

back.en: Elbow flexors (biceps), eccentric.
back.ur: Elbow flexors (biceps), eccentric.

lessonTitle: Muscle Contraction — Concentric, Eccentric, Isometric & Length–Tension

front.en: Order of maximal force by contraction type?
front.ur: Contraction type ke hisaab se maximal force ki tarteeb?

back.en: Eccentric > isometric > concentric.
back.ur: Eccentric > isometric > concentric.

lessonTitle: Muscle Contraction — Concentric, Eccentric, Isometric & Length–Tension

front.en: Where on the length–tension curve is active force greatest?
front.ur: Length–tension curve par active force kahan sab se zyada?

back.en: Near resting (mid-range) length, with optimal actin–myosin overlap.
back.ur: Resting (mid-range) length ke qareeb, behtareen actin–myosin overlap par.

lessonTitle: Muscle Contraction — Concentric, Eccentric, Isometric & Length–Tension

front.en: When is the sprinting hamstring most at risk, and how?
front.ur: Sprint mein hamstring kab sab se zyada risk mein hota hai, aur kaise?

back.en: Late swing — high-force eccentric braking at long length.
back.ur: Late swing — lambi length par high-force eccentric braking.

lessonTitle: Levers, Torque & Moment Arms — Biomechanics You Actually Use

front.en: Formula for torque?
front.ur: Torque ka formula?

back.en: Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the axis (moment arm).
back.ur: Torque = force × axis se perpendicular faasla (moment arm).

lessonTitle: Levers, Torque & Moment Arms — Biomechanics You Actually Use

front.en: What's in the middle in 1st, 2nd and 3rd class levers?
front.ur: 1st, 2nd aur 3rd class levers mein beech mein kya hai?

back.en: Fulcrum, Load, Effort (FLE 1-2-3).
back.ur: Fulcrum, Load, Effort (FLE 1-2-3).

lessonTitle: Levers, Torque & Moment Arms — Biomechanics You Actually Use

front.en: Most common lever class in the body, and what it favours?
front.ur: Jism mein sab se aam lever class, aur kis cheez ko favour karti hai?

back.en: 3rd class — favours speed and range of motion over force.
back.ur: 3rd class — force ke bajaye speed aur range of motion.

lessonTitle: Levers, Torque & Moment Arms — Biomechanics You Actually Use

front.en: Which hand for a cane in hip OA, and why?
front.ur: Hip OA mein cane kis haath mein, aur kyun?

back.en: Opposite hand — creates a long counter-moment that reduces hip abductor force and joint compression.
back.ur: Opposite haath — lamba counter-moment banata hai jo hip abductor force aur joint compression kam karta hai.

lessonTitle: Levers, Torque & Moment Arms — Biomechanics You Actually Use

front.en: Name two ways to make a shoulder abduction exercise easier.
front.ur: Shoulder abduction exercise asaan karne ke do tareeqe?

back.en: Bend the elbow (shorter lever) or hold the weight closer to the shoulder; or reduce gravity's effect.
back.ur: Elbow morein (chhota lever) ya weight shoulder ke qareeb pakrein; ya gravity ka asar kam karein.

lessonTitle: Open vs Closed Kinetic Chain — The Foot Decides

front.en: Define an open kinetic chain exercise.
front.ur: Open kinetic chain exercise ki definition?

back.en: The distal segment (hand/foot) is free to move in space — e.g. seated knee extension.
back.ur: Distal hissa (hand/foot) hawa mein azaad — maslan baith kar knee extension.

lessonTitle: Open vs Closed Kinetic Chain — The Foot Decides

front.en: Define a closed kinetic chain exercise.
front.ur: Closed kinetic chain exercise ki definition?

back.en: The distal segment is fixed and the body moves over it — e.g. squat, push-up.
back.ur: Distal hissa fixed aur body us ke upar move kare — maslan squat, push-up.

lessonTitle: Open vs Closed Kinetic Chain — The Foot Decides

front.en: Main advantage of closed chain exercise?
front.ur: Closed chain exercise ka asal faida?

back.en: Multi-joint, co-contraction, closer to functional tasks like standing up and stairs.
back.ur: Multi-joint, co-contraction, uthne aur seerhiyon jaise functional kaamon ke qareeb.

lessonTitle: Open vs Closed Kinetic Chain — The Foot Decides

front.en: Open-chain knee extension after ACL reconstruction?
front.ur: ACL reconstruction ke baad open-chain knee extension?

back.en: Can be used — introduced in a restricted range (commonly 90°–45°) and progressed per the surgeon's protocol.
back.ur: Use ho sakti hai — mehdood range (aam tor par 90°–45°) mein shuru, surgeon ke protocol ke mutabiq barhayein.

front.en: Classic scapulohumeral rhythm ratio?
front.ur: Classic scapulohumeral rhythm ratio?

back.en: About 2:1 glenohumeral to scapulothoracic (≈120°:60° over full elevation).
back.ur: Taqreeban 2:1 glenohumeral to scapulothoracic (poori elevation par ≈120°:60°).

front.en: Three scapular motions during arm elevation?
front.ur: Arm elevation mein scapula ki teen movements?

back.en: Upward rotation, posterior tilt, external rotation.
back.ur: Upward rotation, posterior tilt, external rotation.

front.en: Muscles of the scapular upward rotation force couple?
front.ur: Scapular upward rotation force couple ki muscles?

back.en: Upper trapezius, lower trapezius, serratus anterior.
back.ur: Upper trapezius, lower trapezius, serratus anterior.

front.en: Medial winging on pushing — which nerve?
front.ur: Push karte waqt medial winging — kaun si nerve?

back.en: Long thoracic nerve (serratus anterior).
back.ur: Long thoracic nerve (serratus anterior).

front.en: What does the scapular assistance test do?
front.ur: Scapular assistance test kya karta hai?

back.en: Assists upward rotation/posterior tilt during elevation; less pain or more range suggests a scapular contribution.
back.ur: Elevation ke dauraan upward rotation/posterior tilt mein madad; dard kam ya range zyada = scapula ka hissa.

front.en: Stance vs swing at normal speed?
front.ur: Normal raftaar par stance vs swing?

back.en: About 60% stance, 40% swing.
back.ur: Taqreeban 60% stance, 40% swing.

front.en: Name the 5 stance phases.
front.ur: Stance ke 5 phases?

back.en: Initial contact, loading response, mid stance, terminal stance, pre-swing.
back.ur: Initial contact, loading response, mid stance, terminal stance, pre-swing.

front.en: Foot slap after heel strike suggests weakness of…?
front.ur: Heel ke baad foot slap kis ki weakness batata hai?

back.en: Dorsiflexors (tibialis anterior) — they lower the foot eccentrically in loading response.
back.ur: Dorsiflexors (tibialis anterior) — yeh loading response mein foot ko eccentric tareeqe se neeche laate hain.

front.en: Pelvis drops on the left while standing on the right leg → weak…?
front.ur: Right leg par khare hone par left pelvis gire → weak…?

back.en: Right hip abductors (gluteus medius) — positive Trendelenburg.
back.ur: Right hip abductors (gluteus medius) — positive Trendelenburg.

front.en: What is double support?
front.ur: Double support kya hai?

back.en: When both feet are on the ground — at the start and end of stance; it disappears in running.
back.ur: Jab dono feet zameen par hon — stance ke shuru aur end par; daurne mein khatam.

lessonTitle: Tissue Healing Phases — What to Do and When

front.en: Name the three phases of soft-tissue healing.
front.ur: Soft-tissue healing ke teen phases?

back.en: Inflammatory → proliferative (repair) → remodelling (maturation). They overlap.
back.ur: Inflammatory → proliferative (repair) → remodelling (maturation). Yeh overlap karte hain.

lessonTitle: Tissue Healing Phases — What to Do and When

front.en: What happens in the proliferative phase?
front.ur: Proliferative phase mein kya hota hai?

back.en: Fibroblasts lay down new (initially weaker, disorganised) collagen and new blood vessels form.
back.ur: Fibroblasts naya (shuru mein weak, be-tarteeb) collagen banate hain aur nayi blood vessels banti hain.

lessonTitle: Tissue Healing Phases — What to Do and When

front.en: What happens in remodelling?
front.ur: Remodelling mein kya hota hai?

back.en: Collagen matures and aligns along lines of stress; strength rises slowly over months.
back.ur: Collagen pakka hota hai aur stress ki lines ke saath seedha hota hai; mazbooti mahinon mein aahista barhti hai.

lessonTitle: Tissue Healing Phases — What to Do and When

front.en: What does PEACE & LOVE stand for?
front.ur: PEACE & LOVE ka matlab?

back.en: Protect, Elevate, Avoid anti-inflammatory modalities, Compress, Educate & Load, Optimism, Vascularisation, Exercise.
back.ur: Protect, Elevate, Avoid anti-inflammatory modalities, Compress, Educate & Load, Optimism, Vascularisation, Exercise.

lessonTitle: Tissue Healing Phases — What to Do and When

front.en: Is 'pain-free' enough to return to sport?
front.ur: Kya 'dard se azaad' hona sport mein wapsi ke liye kaafi hai?

back.en: No — use strength and functional criteria; tissue keeps remodelling for months.
back.ur: Nahi — strength aur functional criteria use karein; tissue mahinon tak remodel hota hai.

lessonTitle: Tendinopathy & Load Management — Why Rest Fails and Loading Works

front.en: Three stages of the tendinopathy continuum?
front.ur: Tendinopathy continuum ke teen stages?

back.en: Reactive, tendon dysrepair, degenerative (Cook & Purdam).
back.ur: Reactive, tendon dysrepair, degenerative (Cook & Purdam).

lessonTitle: Tendinopathy & Load Management — Why Rest Fails and Loading Works

front.en: The pain-monitoring model rules?
front.ur: Pain-monitoring model ke rules?

back.en: Pain ≤5/10 during, settled by next morning, not increasing week to week.
back.ur: Dauraan dard ≤5/10, agli subah tak settle, hafta ba hafta na barhe.

lessonTitle: Tendinopathy & Load Management — Why Rest Fails and Loading Works

front.en: Heavy slow resistance — typical dose?
front.ur: Heavy slow resistance — aam dose?

back.en: 3–4 sets, ~3 s up/3 s down, progressing ~15RM → 6RM, 3×/week for 12+ weeks.
back.ur: 3–4 sets, ~3 s upar/3 s neeche, ~15RM → 6RM, hafte mein 3 dafa, 12+ hafte.

lessonTitle: Tendinopathy & Load Management — Why Rest Fails and Loading Works

front.en: Long-term effect of corticosteroid injection for lateral elbow tendinopathy?
front.ur: Lateral elbow tendinopathy mein corticosteroid injection ka long-term asar?

back.en: Short-term relief but worse 1-year outcomes and more recurrence (Coombes 2013).
back.ur: Thori dair aaram lekin 1 saal par badtar nataij aur zyada recurrence (Coombes 2013).

lessonTitle: Tendinopathy & Load Management — Why Rest Fails and Loading Works

front.en: Which test screens for Achilles rupture?
front.ur: Achilles rupture ke liye kaun sa test?

back.en: Thompson (calf squeeze) test — no plantarflexion = positive.
back.ur: Thompson (calf squeeze) test — plantarflexion na ho = positive.

lessonTitle: Exercise Dosage — FITT, RPE & Reps in Reserve

front.en: What does FITT-VP stand for?
front.ur: FITT-VP ka matlab?

back.en: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type, Volume, Progression.
back.ur: Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type, Volume, Progression.

lessonTitle: Exercise Dosage — FITT, RPE & Reps in Reserve

front.en: Moderate aerobic intensity on the Borg 6–20 scale and talk test?
front.ur: Borg 6–20 aur talk test par darmiyani aerobic intensity?

back.en: About RPE 12–13: can talk in sentences but can't sing.
back.ur: Taqreeban RPE 12–13: jumlon mein baat kar sakte hain, gaa nahi sakte.

lessonTitle: Exercise Dosage — FITT, RPE & Reps in Reserve

front.en: What is "reps in reserve" (RIR)?
front.ur: "Reps in reserve" (RIR) kya hai?

back.en: How many more good-form reps could have been done at the end of the set.
back.ur: Set ke end par achi form ke saath kitne aur reps ho sakte thay.

lessonTitle: Exercise Dosage — FITT, RPE & Reps in Reserve

front.en: Typical novice strength dose?
front.ur: Naye insaan ki aam strength dose?

back.en: 2–3 days/week, 1–3 sets of 8–12 reps at ~60–70% 1RM, ending ~1–3 RIR.
back.ur: Hafte mein 2–3 din, 1–3 sets, 8–12 reps, ~60–70% 1RM, end par ~1–3 RIR.

lessonTitle: Exercise Dosage — FITT, RPE & Reps in Reserve

front.en: WHO 2020 aerobic activity for adults?
front.ur: WHO 2020 adults ke liye aerobic activity?

back.en: 150–300 min/week moderate or 75–150 min vigorous (or a combination), plus strengthening 2+ days/week.
back.ur: Hafte mein 150–300 min darmiyani ya 75–150 min shadeed (ya dono mila kar), saath 2+ din strengthening.

lessonTitle: Subjective Assessment — SIN, Irritability & the 24-Hour Pattern

front.en: What does SIN stand for?
front.ur: SIN ka matlab?

back.en: Severity, Irritability, Nature.
back.ur: Severity, Irritability, Nature.

lessonTitle: Subjective Assessment — SIN, Irritability & the 24-Hour Pattern

front.en: Three parts of irritability?
front.ur: Irritability ke teen hisse?

back.en: How little activity provokes it, how severe it gets, how long it takes to settle.
back.ur: Kitni kam activity se bharakta hai, kitna shadeed hota hai, settle hone mein kitna waqt.

lessonTitle: Subjective Assessment — SIN, Irritability & the 24-Hour Pattern

front.en: Morning stiffness suggesting inflammatory pain?
front.ur: Kitni morning stiffness inflammatory pain ki taraf ishara karti hai?

back.en: More than about 30 minutes, easing with movement.
back.ur: Taqreeban 30 minute se zyada, movement se behtar.

lessonTitle: Subjective Assessment — SIN, Irritability & the 24-Hour Pattern

front.en: How do you examine a highly irritable patient?
front.ur: Highly irritable patient ko kaise examine karein?

back.en: Only essential tests, stop at first pain (P1), few repetitions, no overpressure; re-test after gentle treatment.
back.ur: Sirf zaroori tests, pehle dard (P1) par rukein, kam repetitions, overpressure nahi; gentle treatment ke baad re-test.

lessonTitle: Subjective Assessment — SIN, Irritability & the 24-Hour Pattern

front.en: Name four special-question red flags.
front.ur: Chaar special-question red flags batayein.

back.en: Any four of: history of cancer, unexplained weight loss, fever, unrelenting night pain, saddle anaesthesia/bladder or bowel change, progressive neuro deficit, major trauma, long-term steroids.
back.ur: Koi bhi chaar: cancer history, be-wajah weight loss, bukhar, na rukne wala night pain, saddle anaesthesia/bladder ya bowel change, barhta neuro deficit, bara trauma, lambe arse tak steroids.

lessonTitle: End-Feel, Capsular Patterns & Selective Tissue Tension

front.en: Three normal end-feels with an example each?
front.ur: Teen normal end-feels, har ek ki misaal?

back.en: Soft (knee flexion), firm (shoulder ER), hard (elbow extension).
back.ur: Soft (knee flexion), firm (shoulder ER), hard (elbow extension).

lessonTitle: End-Feel, Capsular Patterns & Selective Tissue Tension

front.en: What is an empty end-feel and why does it matter?
front.ur: Empty end-feel kya hai aur kyun aham?

back.en: Pain stops movement before any resistance is felt — suggests acute bursitis or serious pathology; don't force, investigate/refer.
back.ur: Kisi resistance se pehle dard movement rok deta hai — acute bursitis ya serious pathology; zor na dein, investigate/refer karein.

lessonTitle: End-Feel, Capsular Patterns & Selective Tissue Tension

front.en: Shoulder capsular pattern?
front.ur: Shoulder capsular pattern?

back.en: External rotation > abduction > internal rotation.
back.ur: External rotation > abduction > internal rotation.

lessonTitle: End-Feel, Capsular Patterns & Selective Tissue Tension

front.en: Knee and hip capsular patterns?
front.ur: Knee aur hip capsular patterns?

back.en: Knee: flexion > extension. Hip: internal rotation most, then flexion and abduction.
back.ur: Knee: flexion > extension. Hip: sab se zyada internal rotation, phir flexion aur abduction.

lessonTitle: End-Feel, Capsular Patterns & Selective Tissue Tension

front.en: Resisted test weak & painless — think?
front.ur: Resisted test weak & painless — kya sochein?

back.en: Complete rupture or a neurological cause.
back.ur: Mukammal rupture ya neurological wajah.

front.en: Maitland Grade I?
front.ur: Maitland Grade I?

back.en: Small amplitude at the beginning of the range.
back.ur: Range ke shuru mein chhoti movement.

front.en: Maitland Grade II?
front.ur: Maitland Grade II?

back.en: Large amplitude within the range, not reaching resistance.
back.ur: Range ke andar bari movement, resistance tak nahi.

front.en: Maitland Grade III?
front.ur: Maitland Grade III?

back.en: Large amplitude into resistance, up to the limit.
back.ur: Resistance ke andar limit tak bari movement.

front.en: Maitland Grade IV?
front.ur: Maitland Grade IV?

back.en: Small amplitude at the limit, into resistance.
back.ur: Limit par, resistance ke andar chhoti movement.

front.en: Maitland Grade V?
front.ur: Maitland Grade V?

back.en: Small-amplitude, high-velocity thrust at the end of available range (manipulation).
back.ur: Available range ke end par chhota, tez thrust (manipulation).

front.en: Pain-dominant vs stiffness-dominant joint: which grades?
front.ur: Dard-dominant vs stiffness-dominant joint: kaun se grades?

back.en: Pain/irritable → I–II. Stiffness → III–IV. Reassess every set.
back.ur: Dard/irritable → I–II. Stiffness → III–IV. Har set reassess.

front.en: Define sensitivity.
front.ur: Sensitivity ki definition?

back.en: The proportion of people WITH the condition who test positive (true positive rate).
back.ur: Jin logon ko condition HAI un mein se kitne positive aate hain (true positive rate).

front.en: Define specificity.
front.ur: Specificity ki definition?

back.en: The proportion of people WITHOUT the condition who test negative (true negative rate).
back.ur: Jin logon ko condition NAHI un mein se kitne negative aate hain (true negative rate).

front.en: What does SnNout mean?
front.ur: SnNout ka matlab?

back.en: High Sensitivity + Negative result → helps rule the condition OUT.
back.ur: High Sensitivity + Negative result → condition rule OUT karne mein madad.

front.en: What does SpPin mean?
front.ur: SpPin ka matlab?

back.en: High Specificity + Positive result → helps rule the condition IN.
back.ur: High Specificity + Positive result → condition rule IN karne mein madad.

front.en: Rough thresholds for strong likelihood ratios?
front.ur: Strong likelihood ratios ki andaazan hadd?

back.en: LR+ > 10 (strong for ruling in); LR− < 0.1 (strong for ruling out).
back.ur: LR+ > 10 (rule in ke liye strong); LR− < 0.1 (rule out ke liye strong).

lessonTitle: Red Flags — When NOT to Treat (and What to Do Instead)

front.en: Cauda equina syndrome warning signs?
front.ur: Cauda equina syndrome ke warning signs?

back.en: Saddle numbness, new bladder/bowel dysfunction, bilateral leg symptoms, sexual dysfunction → same-day emergency.
back.ur: Saddle numbness, bladder/bowel ki nayi kharabi, dono legs mein symptoms, sexual dysfunction → usi din emergency.

lessonTitle: Red Flags — When NOT to Treat (and What to Do Instead)

front.en: The 5 Ds and 3 Ns?
front.ur: 5 Ds aur 3 Ns?

back.en: Dizziness, Diplopia, Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Drop attacks · Nystagmus, Nausea, Numbness.
back.ur: Dizziness, Diplopia, Dysarthria, Dysphagia, Drop attacks · Nystagmus, Nausea, Numbness.

lessonTitle: Red Flags — When NOT to Treat (and What to Do Instead)

front.en: Strongest single clue for spinal malignancy?
front.ur: Spinal malignancy ka sab se mazboot akela ishara?

back.en: A past history of cancer.
back.ur: Cancer ki purani history.

lessonTitle: Red Flags — When NOT to Treat (and What to Do Instead)

front.en: Red flag vs yellow flag?
front.ur: Red flag vs yellow flag?

back.en: Red = possible serious pathology (refer). Yellow = psychosocial barriers to recovery (address in care).
back.ur: Red = mumkina serious pathology (refer). Yellow = recovery ki psychosocial rukawatein (care mein address).

lessonTitle: Red Flags — When NOT to Treat (and What to Do Instead)

front.en: Why look for clusters of red flags?
front.ur: Red flags ke clusters kyun dekhein?

back.en: Single flags have poor accuracy on their own; combinations plus the story are more informative.
back.ur: Akele flags ki accuracy weak hai; combinations aur kahani zyada maloomat dete hain.

lessonTitle: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

front.en: L4 myotome, dermatome and reflex?
front.ur: L4 myotome, dermatome aur reflex?

back.en: Ankle dorsiflexion · medial leg/medial malleolus · knee jerk (mainly L4).
back.ur: Ankle dorsiflexion · leg ka andar wala hissa/medial malleolus · knee jerk (zyada L4).

lessonTitle: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

front.en: L5 myotome and dermatome?
front.ur: L5 myotome aur dermatome?

back.en: Great-toe extension · dorsum of the foot (no reliable routine reflex).
back.ur: Big toe ki extension · foot ki upar wali surface (reliable routine reflex nahi).

lessonTitle: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

front.en: S1 myotome, dermatome and reflex?
front.ur: S1 myotome, dermatome aur reflex?

back.en: Plantarflexion/eversion · lateral foot & heel · ankle jerk.
back.ur: Plantarflexion/eversion · foot aur heel ka bahar wala hissa · ankle jerk.

lessonTitle: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

front.en: C6 myotome, dermatome and reflex?
front.ur: C6 myotome, dermatome aur reflex?

back.en: Elbow flexion & wrist extension · lateral forearm & thumb · brachioradialis (and biceps C5–6).
back.ur: Elbow flexion aur wrist extension · forearm ka bahar wala hissa aur thumb · brachioradialis (aur biceps C5–6).

lessonTitle: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

front.en: C7 myotome, dermatome and reflex?
front.ur: C7 myotome, dermatome aur reflex?

back.en: Elbow extension & wrist flexion · middle finger · triceps jerk.
back.ur: Elbow extension aur wrist flexion · middle finger · triceps jerk.

lessonTitle: Dermatomes, Myotomes & Reflexes — The Neuro Screen Made Easy

front.en: What is the Jendrassik manoeuvre for?
front.ur: Jendrassik manoeuvre kis liye?

back.en: Reinforcement to bring out a lower-limb reflex that seems absent (patient pulls hooked fingers apart).
back.ur: Ghayab lagte lower-limb reflex ko ubharne ke liye reinforcement (patient interlocked fingers zor se kheenchta hai).

lessonTitle: UMN vs LMN Lesions — Never Confuse Them Again

front.en: Where does the lower motor neuron start?
front.ur: Lower motor neuron kahan se shuru hota hai?

back.en: In the anterior horn of the spinal cord (or a cranial nerve motor nucleus), travelling out to the muscle.
back.ur: Spinal cord ke anterior horn (ya cranial nerve motor nucleus) se, muscle tak.

lessonTitle: UMN vs LMN Lesions — Never Confuse Them Again

front.en: Tone and reflexes in a UMN lesion?
front.ur: UMN lesion mein tone aur reflexes?

back.en: Increased tone (spasticity) and brisk reflexes; extensor plantar response.
back.ur: Tone barha hua (spasticity), reflexes tez; extensor plantar response.

lessonTitle: UMN vs LMN Lesions — Never Confuse Them Again

front.en: Tone, reflexes and bulk in an LMN lesion?
front.ur: LMN lesion mein tone, reflexes aur bulk?

back.en: Flaccid tone, reduced/absent reflexes, early marked wasting; fasciculations possible.
back.ur: Flaccid tone, reflexes kam/ghayab, jaldi wazeh wasting; fasciculations mumkin.

lessonTitle: UMN vs LMN Lesions — Never Confuse Them Again

front.en: Spasticity vs rigidity — the key difference?
front.ur: Spasticity vs rigidity — asal farq?

back.en: Spasticity is velocity-dependent (clasp-knife); rigidity is independent of speed (lead-pipe/cogwheel).
back.ur: Spasticity velocity-dependent (clasp-knife); rigidity raftaar se azad (lead-pipe/cogwheel).

lessonTitle: UMN vs LMN Lesions — Never Confuse Them Again

front.en: Floppy limb on day 1 after stroke — LMN lesion?
front.ur: Stroke ke pehle din dheela limb — LMN lesion?

back.en: No. An early flaccid phase can occur after UMN lesions; spasticity often develops later.
back.ur: Nahi. UMN lesion ke baad shuru mein flaccid phase ho sakta hai; spasticity aksar baad mein aati hai.

lessonTitle: Motor Learning & Neuroplasticity — How Patients Really Relearn Movement

front.en: Performance vs learning?
front.ur: Performance vs learning?

back.en: Performance = during practice; learning = relatively permanent change seen on retention or transfer tests.
back.ur: Performance = practice ke dauraan; learning = nisbatan pakki tabdeeli jo retention ya transfer tests par dikhe.

lessonTitle: Motor Learning & Neuroplasticity — How Patients Really Relearn Movement

front.en: Three stages of motor learning?
front.ur: Motor learning ke teen stages?

back.en: Cognitive, associative, autonomous (Fitts & Posner).
back.ur: Cognitive, associative, autonomous (Fitts & Posner).

lessonTitle: Motor Learning & Neuroplasticity — How Patients Really Relearn Movement

front.en: What is the contextual interference effect?
front.ur: Contextual interference effect kya hai?

back.en: Random/variable practice lowers in-session performance but improves retention and transfer compared with blocked practice.
back.ur: Random/variable practice session ki performance kam karti hai lekin blocked ke muqable retention aur transfer behtar.

lessonTitle: Motor Learning & Neuroplasticity — How Patients Really Relearn Movement

front.en: KR vs KP feedback?
front.ur: KR vs KP feedback?

back.en: Knowledge of results = outcome; knowledge of performance = quality of the movement.
back.ur: Knowledge of results = nateeja; knowledge of performance = movement ka maiyaar.

lessonTitle: Motor Learning & Neuroplasticity — How Patients Really Relearn Movement

front.en: Name five Kleim & Jones neuroplasticity principles.
front.ur: Kleim & Jones ke paanch neuroplasticity usool?

back.en: Any five: use it or lose it, use it and improve it, specificity, repetition, intensity, time, salience, age, transference, interference.
back.ur: Koi paanch: use it or lose it, use it and improve it, specificity, repetition, intensity, time, salience, age, transference, interference.

lessonTitle: Balance Systems & Falls Assessment — From Romberg to TUG

front.en: Three sensory systems for balance?
front.ur: Balance ke teen sensory systems?

back.en: Visual, vestibular, somatosensory (proprioception).
back.ur: Visual, vestibular, somatosensory (proprioception).

lessonTitle: Balance Systems & Falls Assessment — From Romberg to TUG

front.en: What does a positive Romberg test mean?
front.ur: Positive Romberg test ka matlab?

back.en: Stable with eyes open but not closed — proprioceptive (sensory) loss, not cerebellar.
back.ur: Aankhein khuli par stable lekin band par nahi — proprioceptive (sensory) kami, cerebellar nahi.

lessonTitle: Balance Systems & Falls Assessment — From Romberg to TUG

front.en: Common TUG cut-off for higher falls risk in older adults?
front.ur: Buzurgon mein zyada falls risk ke liye aam TUG cut-off?

back.en: About ≥ 12–13.5 seconds (interpret with other findings).
back.ur: Taqreeban ≥ 12–13.5 second (doosri findings ke saath parhein).

lessonTitle: Balance Systems & Falls Assessment — From Romberg to TUG

front.en: Berg Balance Scale maximum and common risk cut-off?
front.ur: Berg Balance Scale ka maximum aur aam risk cut-off?

back.en: 56; below about 45 suggests higher falls risk.
back.ur: 56; taqreeban 45 se kam zyada falls risk batata hai.

lessonTitle: Balance Systems & Falls Assessment — From Romberg to TUG

front.en: Effective falls-prevention exercise dose?
front.ur: Effective falls-prevention exercise dose?

back.en: Progressive, highly challenging balance (+ strength) training, about 3+ hours per week in total, continued.
back.ur: Progressive, zyada challenge wali balance (+ strength) training, hafte mein kul taqreeban 3+ ghante, jaari.

lessonTitle: Pain Science Basics — Why Hurt ≠ Harm

front.en: IASP (2020) definition of pain?
front.ur: IASP (2020) ki dard ki definition?

back.en: An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with, or resembling that associated with, actual or potential tissue damage.
back.ur: An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with, or resembling that associated with, actual or potential tissue damage.

lessonTitle: Pain Science Basics — Why Hurt ≠ Harm

front.en: Nociception vs pain?
front.ur: Nociception vs dard?

back.en: Nociception = danger signalling from tissues. Pain = the brain's protective experience; neither guarantees the other.
back.ur: Nociception = tissues se khatre ka signal. Dard = dimagh ka hifazati tajurba; aik doosre ki zamanat nahi.

lessonTitle: Pain Science Basics — Why Hurt ≠ Harm

front.en: What does the 'nail through the boot' case show?
front.ur: 'Boot mein keel' wala case kya dikhata hai?

back.en: Severe, real pain can occur with no tissue damage.
back.ur: Shadeed, asli dard bina tissue damage ke bhi ho sakta hai.

lessonTitle: Pain Science Basics — Why Hurt ≠ Harm

front.en: A simple, evidence-informed phrase for patients?
front.ur: Patients ke liye ek asaan, evidence-informed jumla?

back.en: "Hurt doesn't always mean harm — we'll build up step by step."
back.ur: "Har dard nuqsan nahi hota — hum qadam ba qadam barhenge."

lessonTitle: TENS & Therapeutic Ultrasound — Parameters, Safety & What the Evidence Really Says

front.en: Conventional TENS parameters?
front.ur: Conventional TENS parameters?

back.en: ~50–120 Hz, short pulse width, strong but comfortable, no muscle twitch.
back.ur: ~50–120 Hz, chhoti pulse width, strong lekin aaramdeh, muscle twitch nahi.

lessonTitle: TENS & Therapeutic Ultrasound — Parameters, Safety & What the Evidence Really Says

front.en: Acupuncture-like TENS parameters and proposed mechanism?
front.ur: Acupuncture-like TENS parameters aur mechanism?

back.en: ~2–4 Hz, higher intensity with visible twitches; may release endogenous opioids.
back.ur: ~2–4 Hz, zyada intensity aur nazar aane wali twitches; endogenous opioids nikal sakte hain.

lessonTitle: TENS & Therapeutic Ultrasound — Parameters, Safety & What the Evidence Really Says

front.en: What did the meta-TENS review conclude?
front.ur: Meta-TENS review ka nateeja?

back.en: Moderate-certainty evidence that pain is lower during or immediately after TENS than placebo.
back.ur: Moderate-certainty evidence ke TENS ke dauraan ya foran baad dard placebo se kam hota hai.

lessonTitle: TENS & Therapeutic Ultrasound — Parameters, Safety & What the Evidence Really Says

front.en: Four TENS contraindications?
front.ur: TENS ke chaar contraindications?

back.en: Any four: demand pacemaker/implanted device, anterior neck/carotid sinus, over pregnant uterus, over eyes, broken or insensate skin, unable to understand.
back.ur: Koi chaar: demand pacemaker/implanted device, anterior neck/carotid sinus, pregnant uterus par, aankhon par, kati ya sunn skin, samajh na sakne wala patient.

lessonTitle: TENS & Therapeutic Ultrasound — Parameters, Safety & What the Evidence Really Says

front.en: Ultrasound: continuous vs pulsed, 1 vs 3 MHz?
front.ur: Ultrasound: continuous vs pulsed, 1 vs 3 MHz?

back.en: Continuous = thermal, pulsed = non-thermal; 1 MHz deeper, 3 MHz superficial.
back.ur: Continuous = thermal, pulsed = non-thermal; 1 MHz gehra, 3 MHz upar upar.

lessonTitle: Airway Clearance — The Active Cycle of Breathing Technique (ACBT)

front.en: Four components of ACBT?
front.ur: ACBT ke chaar hisse?

back.en: Breathing control, thoracic expansion exercises, breathing control, forced expiration technique (huffs).
back.ur: Breathing control, thoracic expansion exercises, breathing control, forced expiration technique (huffs).

lessonTitle: Airway Clearance — The Active Cycle of Breathing Technique (ACBT)

front.en: Low-volume vs high-volume huff?
front.ur: Low-volume vs high-volume huff?

back.en: From a medium breath to move peripheral secretions; from a big breath to clear upper airways.
back.ur: Darmiyani saans se door ki balgham hilane ke liye; bari saans se upar ki airways saaf karne ke liye.

lessonTitle: Airway Clearance — The Active Cycle of Breathing Technique (ACBT)

front.en: Why add a breath hold to thoracic expansion?
front.ur: Thoracic expansion mein saans kyun rokein?

back.en: Allows collateral ventilation to get air behind secretions.
back.ur: Collateral ventilation se hawa balgham ke peeche pohanchti hai.

lessonTitle: Airway Clearance — The Active Cycle of Breathing Technique (ACBT)

front.en: When to stop airway clearance immediately?
front.ur: Airway clearance foran kab rokein?

back.en: Frank haemoptysis, suspected pneumothorax, SpO₂ falling without recovery, new arrhythmia or a deteriorating patient.
back.ur: Wazeh haemoptysis, mumkin pneumothorax, SpO₂ girna aur wapas na aana, nayi arrhythmia ya bigarta patient.

lessonTitle: Airway Clearance — The Active Cycle of Breathing Technique (ACBT)

front.en: Typical ACBT session length?
front.ur: ACBT session ki aam lambai?

back.en: About 10–30 minutes, until two consecutive cycles produce no sputum or the patient tires.
back.ur: Taqreeban 10–30 minute, jab tak lagatar do cycles mein balgham na nikle ya patient thak jaye.

lessonTitle: Sensory Exam & Dermatomes — Find the Level by Touch

front.en: Which fingers does C6, C7 and C8 supply?
front.ur: C6, C7 aur C8 kaun si fingers ko supply karti hain?

back.en: C6 thumb + index, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger (the "6-7-8" hand trick).
back.ur: C6 thumb + index, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger (“6-7-8” hand trick).

lessonTitle: Sensory Exam & Dermatomes — Find the Level by Touch

front.en: Key sensory point for L5?
front.ur: L5 ka key sensory point?

back.en: The top of the foot at the 3rd metatarsophalangeal joint (dorsum of the foot).
back.ur: Foot ka top, 3rd metatarsophalangeal joint par (dorsum of the foot).

lessonTitle: Sensory Exam & Dermatomes — Find the Level by Touch

front.en: Why test both light touch and pinprick?
front.ur: Light touch aur pinprick dono kyun test karte hain?

back.en: They travel in different tracts (dorsal column vs spinothalamic), so a difference between them helps localise a lesion.
back.ur: Yeh alag tracts (dorsal column vs spinothalamic) se guzarti hain, is liye dono ka farq lesion localise karne mein madad deta hai.

lessonTitle: Sensory Exam & Dermatomes — Find the Level by Touch

front.en: What is the sensory level in ISNCSCI?
front.ur: ISNCSCI mein sensory level kya hota hai?

back.en: The most caudal (lowest) dermatome with normal (score 2) light touch and pinprick on that side.
back.ur: Sab se neechla (caudal) dermatome jis mein us side par light touch aur pinprick normal (score 2) hon.

lessonTitle: Sensory Exam & Dermatomes — Find the Level by Touch

front.en: Which tool checks protective sensation in the diabetic foot?
front.ur: Diabetic foot mein protective sensation kaun sa tool check karta hai?

back.en: A 10 g (5.07) Semmes–Weinstein monofilament at standard plantar sites.
back.ur: Standard plantar sites par 10 g (5.07) Semmes–Weinstein monofilament.

lessonTitle: Myotome Screening — Which Root Is Weak?

front.en: C5, C6, C7, C8, T1 myotomes?
front.ur: C5, C6, C7, C8, T1 ke myotomes?

back.en: Shoulder abduction; elbow flexion + wrist extension; elbow extension + wrist flexion; finger flexion; finger abduction.
back.ur: Shoulder abduction; elbow flexion + wrist extension; elbow extension + wrist flexion; finger flexion; finger abduction.

lessonTitle: Myotome Screening — Which Root Is Weak?

front.en: L2, L3, L4, L5, S1 myotomes?
front.ur: L2, L3, L4, L5, S1 ke myotomes?

back.en: Hip flexion; knee extension; ankle dorsiflexion; big-toe extension; ankle plantarflexion.
back.ur: Hip flexion; knee extension; ankle dorsiflexion; bare angootay ki extension; ankle plantarflexion.

lessonTitle: Myotome Screening — Which Root Is Weak?

front.en: An L4–L5 posterolateral disc compresses which root?
front.ur: L4–L5 posterolateral disc kaun si root dabati hai?

back.en: L5 (the traversing root). A far-lateral disc at the same level can hit the exiting L4 root.
back.ur: L5 (traversing root). Isi level ki far-lateral disc exiting L4 root ko maar sakti hai.

lessonTitle: Myotome Screening — Which Root Is Weak?

front.en: How do you separate an L5 root lesion from a common fibular nerve palsy?
front.ur: L5 root lesion aur common fibular nerve palsy mein farq kaise karein?

back.en: Test hip abduction and ankle inversion: weak = L5 root; normal = common fibular nerve.
back.ur: Hip abduction aur ankle inversion test karein: kamzor = L5 root; normal = common fibular nerve.

lessonTitle: Deep Tendon Reflexes — Technique, Grading and Reinforcement

front.en: Roots of the biceps, brachioradialis, triceps, knee and ankle reflexes?
front.ur: Biceps, brachioradialis, triceps, knee aur ankle reflexes ki roots?

lessonTitle: Deep Tendon Reflexes — Technique, Grading and Reinforcement

front.en: What is reinforcement and when do you use it?
front.ur: Reinforcement kya hai aur kab use karte hain?

back.en: Jendrassik manoeuvre (clench teeth, hook fingers and pull) to bring out a reflex that seems absent.
back.ur: Jendrassik manoeuvre (daant bhinchna, ungliyan hook kar ke khenchna) jo gayab lagne wala reflex nikalta hai.

lessonTitle: Deep Tendon Reflexes — Technique, Grading and Reinforcement

front.en: What does a brisk reflex with clonus suggest?
front.ur: Clonus ke saath brisk reflex kis ki taraf ishara karta hai?

back.en: An upper motor neuron lesion above the reflex arc.
back.ur: Reflex arc se upar upper motor neuron lesion.

lessonTitle: Deep Tendon Reflexes — Technique, Grading and Reinforcement

front.en: Which reflex pattern suggests peripheral neuropathy?
front.ur: Kaun sa reflex pattern peripheral neuropathy batata hai?

back.en: Reduced or absent ankle jerks first, symmetrically, with distal sensory loss.
back.ur: Pehle ankle jerks kam ya gayab, symmetrically, aur distal sensory loss ke saath.

lessonTitle: UMN Signs at the Bedside — Babinski, Hoffmann, Clonus and the Jaw Jerk

front.en: What is a positive Babinski sign?
front.ur: Positive Babinski sign kya hai?

back.en: Extension of the great toe with fanning of the other toes on stroking the sole — an UMN sign (normal in infants).
back.ur: Sole par stroke karne se bare angootay ki extension aur baqi toes ka phailna — UMN sign (bachon mein normal).

lessonTitle: UMN Signs at the Bedside — Babinski, Hoffmann, Clonus and the Jaw Jerk

front.en: How do you elicit Hoffmann's sign?
front.ur: Hoffmann sign kaise nikalte hain?

back.en: Hold the relaxed middle finger and flick the fingernail downwards; thumb and index finger flex together if positive.
back.ur: Relaxed middle finger ko pakar kar nail ko neeche flick karein; positive ho to thumb aur index saath flex hoti hain.

lessonTitle: UMN Signs at the Bedside — Babinski, Hoffmann, Clonus and the Jaw Jerk

front.en: How many clonus beats are abnormal?
front.ur: Clonus ki kitni beats abnormal hain?

back.en: More than about 5 beats, or beats that continue while the stretch is held (sustained clonus).
back.ur: Takriban 5 se zyada beats, ya jab tak stretch hold ho beats chalti rahein (sustained clonus).

lessonTitle: UMN Signs at the Bedside — Babinski, Hoffmann, Clonus and the Jaw Jerk

front.en: What does a brisk jaw jerk tell you?
front.ur: Brisk jaw jerk kya batata hai?

back.en: A lesion above the pons (bilateral UMN), since the jaw jerk arc passes through the pons (CN V).
back.ur: Pons se upar lesion (bilateral UMN), kyunke jaw jerk ka arc pons (CN V) se guzarta hai.

lessonTitle: Arm Nerve Injuries — Radial, Median, Ulnar, Axillary and More

front.en: Radial nerve lesion at the spiral groove: what do you see?
front.ur: Spiral groove par radial nerve lesion: kya nazar aata hai?

back.en: Wrist drop (cannot extend wrist and fingers), numb first dorsal web space; triceps is spared.
back.ur: Wrist drop (wrist aur fingers extend nahi), pehli dorsal web sunn; triceps mehfooz.

lessonTitle: Arm Nerve Injuries — Radial, Median, Ulnar, Axillary and More

front.en: What causes ape hand?
front.ur: Ape hand kis wajah se hota hai?

back.en: A median nerve lesion (commonly at the carpal tunnel): thumb stays flat in the palm and the thenar muscles waste.
back.ur: Median nerve lesion (aam taur par carpal tunnel): thumb palm mein flat reh jata hai aur thenar muscles waste hote hain.

lessonTitle: Arm Nerve Injuries — Radial, Median, Ulnar, Axillary and More

front.en: What is Froment's sign?
front.ur: Froment sign kya hai?

back.en: A paper held between thumb and index finger: the thumb IP flexes (FPL, median) to compensate for weak adductor pollicis (ulnar).
back.ur: Thumb aur index ke beech kagaz: thumb ka IP flex hota hai (FPL, median) jo kamzor adductor pollicis (ulnar) ki jagah leta hai.

lessonTitle: Arm Nerve Injuries — Radial, Median, Ulnar, Axillary and More

front.en: Which nerve causes medial winging of the scapula?
front.ur: Scapula ki medial winging kaun si nerve se hoti hai?

back.en: The long thoracic nerve (serratus anterior). Lateral winging is the spinal accessory nerve (trapezius).
back.ur: Long thoracic nerve (serratus anterior). Lateral winging spinal accessory nerve (trapezius) se hoti hai.

lessonTitle: Leg Nerve Injuries — Femoral, Sciatic, Fibular, Tibial and Gluteal

front.en: What is the sign of a common fibular nerve palsy?
front.ur: Common fibular nerve palsy ka sign?

back.en: Foot drop with a steppage gait and numbness over the dorsum of the foot and outer shin.
back.ur: Foot drop, steppage gait aur foot ke dorsum aur outer shin ki numbness.

lessonTitle: Leg Nerve Injuries — Femoral, Sciatic, Fibular, Tibial and Gluteal

front.en: What does Trendelenburg's sign show?
front.ur: Trendelenburg sign kya dikhata hai?

back.en: The pelvis drops on the side opposite the stance leg, because the stance-side gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve) is weak.
back.ur: Pelvis stance leg ki opposite side gir jata hai, kyunke stance side ka gluteus medius (superior gluteal nerve) kamzor hai.

lessonTitle: Leg Nerve Injuries — Femoral, Sciatic, Fibular, Tibial and Gluteal

front.en: Which nerve causes the knee to give way on stairs?
front.ur: Seerhiyon par knee ko kaun si nerve jawab dilati hai?

back.en: The femoral nerve (quadriceps weakness), with a lost knee jerk and numb front of the thigh.
back.ur: Femoral nerve (quadriceps ki kamzori), knee jerk gayab aur thigh ka samna sunn.

lessonTitle: Leg Nerve Injuries — Femoral, Sciatic, Fibular, Tibial and Gluteal

front.en: What is meralgia paraesthetica?
front.ur: Meralgia paraesthetica kya hai?

back.en: Compression of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve under the inguinal ligament: burning or numb outer thigh with no weakness.
back.ur: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve ka inguinal ligament ke neeche dabna: outer thigh par jalan ya numbness, kamzori nahi.

lessonTitle: Muscle Tone — Spasticity, Rigidity and the Modified Ashworth Scale

front.en: How do you tell spasticity from rigidity?
front.ur: Spasticity ko rigidity se kaise alag karte hain?

back.en: Spasticity depends on speed (more resistance when faster, with a catch); rigidity is the same at slow and fast speeds.
back.ur: Spasticity speed par depend karti hai (tez par zyada resistance, catch ke saath); rigidity aahista aur tez dono par ek jaisi.

lessonTitle: Muscle Tone — Spasticity, Rigidity and the Modified Ashworth Scale

front.en: Modified Ashworth Scale grades?
front.ur: Modified Ashworth Scale ke grades?

back.en: 0 none; 1 slight catch; 1+ catch then minimal resistance (<half range); 2 marked increase but easy movement; 3 considerable increase; 4 rigid.
back.ur: 0 koi nahi; 1 halka catch; 1+ catch phir minimal resistance (aadhi range se kam); 2 wazeh izafa lekin aasan movement; 3 kaafi izafa; 4 rigid.

lessonTitle: Muscle Tone — Spasticity, Rigidity and the Modified Ashworth Scale

front.en: What do Tardieu R1 and R2 mean?
front.ur: Tardieu R1 aur R2 ka kya matlab?

back.en: R1 = angle of the catch at fast stretch; R2 = full passive range at slow stretch. A big R2 − R1 gap means spasticity, a small gap means contracture.
back.ur: R1 = tez stretch par catch ka angle; R2 = aahista stretch par poori passive range. Bara R2 − R1 gap spasticity, chhota gap contracture.

lessonTitle: Muscle Tone — Spasticity, Rigidity and the Modified Ashworth Scale

front.en: What is cogwheel rigidity?
front.ur: Cogwheel rigidity kya hai?

back.en: Rigidity with a superimposed tremor, felt as rhythmic ratchet-like give; typical of Parkinson's disease.
back.ur: Rigidity ke upar tremor, rhythmic ratchet jaisi dheel; Parkinson’s disease ki tipical nishani.

lessonTitle: The Cerebellar Exam — Finger-Nose, Rapid Movements, Heel-Shin and DANISH

front.en: What does DANISH stand for?
front.ur: DANISH ka kya matlab hai?

back.en: Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia, Nystagmus, Intention tremor, Slurred speech, Hypotonia.
back.ur: Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia, Nystagmus, Intention tremor, Slurred speech, Hypotonia.

lessonTitle: The Cerebellar Exam — Finger-Nose, Rapid Movements, Heel-Shin and DANISH

front.en: Which side of the body does one cerebellar hemisphere control?
front.ur: Ek cerebellar hemisphere jism ki kaun si side control karta hai?

back.en: The same side (ipsilateral).
back.ur: Usi side (ipsilateral).

lessonTitle: The Cerebellar Exam — Finger-Nose, Rapid Movements, Heel-Shin and DANISH

front.en: How do cerebellar and sensory ataxia differ with eyes closed?
front.ur: Aankhein band karne par cerebellar aur sensory ataxia mein kya farq hai?

back.en: Sensory ataxia gets much worse with eyes closed; cerebellar ataxia does not change much.
back.ur: Sensory ataxia aankhein band karne par bohat kharab hoti hai; cerebellar ataxia mein zyada tabdeeli nahi.

lessonTitle: The Cerebellar Exam — Finger-Nose, Rapid Movements, Heel-Shin and DANISH

front.en: What is dysdiadochokinesia?
front.ur: Dysdiadochokinesia kya hai?

back.en: Inability to perform rapid alternating movements smoothly (slow, uneven and clumsy).
back.ur: Rapid alternating movements ko smoothly na kar pana (aahista, be-tarteeb aur anari).

lessonTitle: Romberg, Tandem Gait and Pronator Drift — Three Fast Neuro Screens

front.en: When is Romberg's test positive?
front.ur: Romberg test kab positive hota hai?

back.en: When the patient is steady with eyes open but loses balance with eyes closed (proprioceptive or vestibular loss).
back.ur: Jab patient aankhein khuli hon to steady aur band hon to balance kho de (proprioceptive ya vestibular kami).

lessonTitle: Romberg, Tandem Gait and Pronator Drift — Three Fast Neuro Screens

front.en: What does pronator drift show?
front.ur: Pronator drift kya dikhata hai?

back.en: A subtle corticospinal (upper motor neuron) lesion: the forearm pronates and the arm sinks.
back.ur: Halki corticospinal (upper motor neuron) lesion: forearm pronate hoti hai aur arm dhalta hai.

lessonTitle: Romberg, Tandem Gait and Pronator Drift — Three Fast Neuro Screens

front.en: Which test is the most sensitive bedside test of mild cerebellar disease?
front.ur: Halki cerebellar bimari ka sab se sensitive bedside test?

back.en: Tandem (heel-to-toe) walking.
back.ur: Tandem (heel-to-toe) walking.

lessonTitle: Romberg, Tandem Gait and Pronator Drift — Three Fast Neuro Screens

front.en: Why test with eyes closed?
front.ur: Aankhein band kar ke test kyun karte hain?

back.en: Vision hides proprioceptive and corticospinal deficits; closing the eyes forces the patient to rely on position sense.
back.ur: Vision proprioceptive aur corticospinal kami ko chhupati hai; aankhein band karne se patient ko position sense par bharosa karna parta hai.

lessonTitle: Root, Cord or Nerve? Localising a Neurological Lesion

front.en: Three questions to localise a neurological lesion?
front.ur: Neurological lesion localise karne ke teen sawal?

back.en: Reflexes and tone (UMN or LMN)? Shape of the sensory loss? Which muscles are weak?
back.ur: Reflexes aur tone (UMN ya LMN)? Sensory kami ki shakal? Kaun se muscles kamzor?

lessonTitle: Root, Cord or Nerve? Localising a Neurological Lesion

front.en: What finding pattern suggests cervical myelopathy?
front.ur: Kaun sa finding pattern cervical myelopathy batata hai?

back.en: Clumsy hands, gait change, brisk reflexes, Hoffmann or Babinski, age over 45.
back.ur: Anari haath, gait mein tabdeeli, brisk reflexes, Hoffmann ya Babinski, 45 saal se zyada umar.

lessonTitle: Root, Cord or Nerve? Localising a Neurological Lesion

front.en: Why do ankle jerks go first in polyneuropathy?
front.ur: Polyneuropathy mein ankle jerks pehle kyun jaate hain?

back.en: The longest nerves fail first (length-dependent), so the most distal reflexes and sensation go earliest.
back.ur: Sab se lambi nerves pehle fail hoti hain (length-dependent), is liye sab se distal reflexes aur sensation pehle jaate hain.

lessonTitle: Root, Cord or Nerve? Localising a Neurological Lesion

front.en: What is an inverted supinator sign?
front.ur: Inverted supinator sign kya hai?

back.en: Tapping brachioradialis gives finger flexion but no elbow flexion: a C5–C6 cord lesion (arc damaged at C6, release below).
back.ur: Brachioradialis tap karne par finger flexion lekin elbow flexion nahi: C5–C6 cord lesion (C6 par arc kharab, neeche release).

lessonTitle: Goniometry Foundations — Axis, Arms, Scale and the Six Steps

front.en: What are the six steps of goniometry?
front.ur: Goniometry ke chhe steps?

back.en: Position, stabilise, find landmarks, align, move and measure (re-align), record.
back.ur: Position, stabilise, landmarks dhoondein, align, move aur measure (dobara align), record.

lessonTitle: Goniometry Foundations — Axis, Arms, Scale and the Six Steps

front.en: Where does the stationary arm point?
front.ur: Stationary arm kahan point karti hai?

back.en: Along the proximal segment, aligned on a bony landmark of the segment that does not move.
back.ur: Proximal segment ke saath, us segment ke bony landmark par jo hilta nahi.

lessonTitle: Goniometry Foundations — Axis, Arms, Scale and the Six Steps

front.en: How large is acceptable measurement error?
front.ur: Qabil-e-qabool measurement error kitna hai?

back.en: About 5° for most limb joints; a smaller change may not be real.
back.ur: Zyada tar limb joints ke liye takriban 5°; isse chhoti tabdeeli asli na ho.

lessonTitle: Goniometry Foundations — Axis, Arms, Scale and the Six Steps

front.en: How do you record hip abduction when the dial starts at 90°?
front.ur: Dial 90° se shuru ho to hip abduction kaise likhein?

back.en: Record the change from the start (0–45°), not the dial reading.
back.ur: Start se tabdeeli likhein (0–45°), dial ki reading nahi.

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Shoulder, Elbow and Wrist — Landmarks That Work

front.en: Normal shoulder flexion, extension and abduction?
front.ur: Normal shoulder flexion, extension aur abduction?

back.en: Flexion 0–180°, extension 0–60°, abduction 0–180° (AAOS).
back.ur: Flexion 0–180°, extension 0–60°, abduction 0–180° (AAOS).

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Shoulder, Elbow and Wrist — Landmarks That Work

front.en: Where is the axis for elbow flexion?
front.ur: Elbow flexion ke liye axis kahan hai?

back.en: The lateral epicondyle of the humerus.
back.ur: Humerus ka lateral epicondyle.

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Shoulder, Elbow and Wrist — Landmarks That Work

front.en: Capsular pattern of the glenohumeral joint?
front.ur: Glenohumeral joint ka capsular pattern?

back.en: Greatest loss of external rotation, then abduction, then internal rotation.
back.ur: Sab se zyada kami external rotation, phir abduction, phir internal rotation.

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Shoulder, Elbow and Wrist — Landmarks That Work

front.en: Why keep the fingers relaxed for wrist extension?
front.ur: Wrist extension ke liye fingers relaxed kyun?

back.en: Fully extended fingers tighten the long finger flexors and limit wrist extension.
back.ur: Poori extended fingers long finger flexors ko tight kar ke wrist extension ko limit karti hain.

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Positions That Make It Fair

front.en: Normal hip flexion, abduction, knee flexion and ankle dorsiflexion?
front.ur: Normal hip flexion, abduction, knee flexion aur ankle dorsiflexion?

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Positions That Make It Fair

front.en: Why bend the knee to measure dorsiflexion?
front.ur: Dorsiflexion naapne ke liye knee kyun mor'te hain?

back.en: It slackens the gastrocnemius so that you measure joint range, not muscle length.
back.ur: Gastrocnemius dheela hota hai taake aap joint range naapein, muscle length nahi.

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Positions That Make It Fair

front.en: Where is the axis for hip abduction?
front.ur: Hip abduction ka axis kahan hai?

back.en: Over the ASIS of the tested side.
back.ur: Tested side ke ASIS ke upar.

lessonTitle: Goniometry of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Positions That Make It Fair

front.en: What error inflates hip flexion?
front.ur: Hip flexion ko kaun si ghalti phulati hai?

back.en: A posterior pelvic tilt (lumbar flexion).
back.ur: Posterior pelvic tilt (lumbar flexion).

lessonTitle: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

front.en: Define MMT grades 2 and 3.
front.ur: MMT grades 2 aur 3 define karein.

back.en: Grade 2: full range with gravity eliminated. Grade 3: full range against gravity.
back.ur: Grade 2: gravity hata kar poori range. Grade 3: gravity ke khilaf poori range.

lessonTitle: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

front.en: Where do you apply resistance?
front.ur: Resistance kahan lagate hain?

back.en: At the distal end of the segment the muscle moves, building slowly over 2–3 seconds.
back.ur: Us segment ke distal end par jise muscle hilata hai, 2–3 seconds mein aahista barhate hue.

lessonTitle: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

front.en: What is the weak spot of MMT?
front.ur: MMT ki kamzori kya hai?

back.en: Poor discrimination between grades 4 and 5 and in large strong muscles; use a dynamometer.
back.ur: Grades 4 aur 5 ke beech aur bare mazboot muscles mein kamzor farq; dynamometer use karein.

lessonTitle: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

front.en: When is MMT the wrong tool?
front.ur: MMT kab ghalat tool hai?

back.en: In spasticity, in young children, severe pain or cognitive impairment; use tone, function and observation instead.
back.ur: Spasticity, chhote bachon, shadeed dard ya cognitive impairment mein; iske bajaye tone, function aur observation use karein.

lessonTitle: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

front.en: What does scapular winging with wall push-up suggest?
front.ur: Wall push-up par scapular winging kya batati hai?

back.en: Weak serratus anterior (long thoracic nerve); the medial border lifts off the ribs.
back.ur: Kamzor serratus anterior (long thoracic nerve); medial border ribs se uth jata hai.

lessonTitle: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

front.en: Which muscle substitutes by shrugging in shoulder abduction?
front.ur: Shoulder abduction mein shrug kar ke kaun sa muscle substitute karta hai?

back.en: The upper trapezius.
back.ur: Upper trapezius.

lessonTitle: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

front.en: What is tenodesis?
front.ur: Tenodesis kya hai?

back.en: Passive finger closure on wrist extension (and opening on wrist flexion) from tendon tension; it can fake finger flexion.
back.ur: Wrist extension par fingers ka passively band hona (aur wrist flexion par khulna) tendon tension se; yeh finger flexion ki naqal kar sakta hai.

lessonTitle: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

front.en: Why is a 5/5 not always normal?
front.ur: 5/5 hamesha normal kyun nahi hota?

back.en: Manual testing cannot break a strong muscle, so a 20–50% deficit can hide at grade 5; use a dynamometer.
back.ur: Manual testing mazboot muscle ko tor nahi sakti, is liye 20–50 % kami grade 5 mein chhup sakti hai; dynamometer use karein.

front.en: A very irritable shoulder: which grades and why?
front.ur: A very irritable shoulder: which grades and why?

back.en: Grades I-II. They are small and gentle and aim to calm pain without provoking a flare.
back.ur: Grades I-II. They are small and gentle and aim to calm pain without provoking a flare.

front.en: The joint feels smoother but the patient's neck turn is unchanged. What have you proved?
front.ur: The joint feels smoother but the patient's neck turn is unchanged. What have you proved?

back.en: Only that your hand felt something. Trust the comparable sign, not your feel, and rethink the plan.
back.ur: Only that your hand felt something. Trust the comparable sign, not your feel, and rethink the plan.

front.en: Maitland Joint Mobilization: what does "Comparable sign" mean?
front.ur: Maitland Joint Mobilization: "Comparable sign" ka matlab?

back.en: The one movement or symptom you test before and after treatment, for example neck rotation to the right or shoulder lifting to 90 degrees.
back.ur: The one movement or symptom you test before and after treatment, for example neck rotation to the right or shoulder lifting to 90 degrees.

front.en: Maitland Joint Mobilization: what does "Accessory movement" mean?
front.ur: Maitland Joint Mobilization: "Accessory movement" ka matlab?

back.en: A tiny joint glide the patient cannot do on their own, such as one vertebra gliding forward. You produce it with your hands.
back.ur: A tiny joint glide the patient cannot do on their own, such as one vertebra gliding forward. You produce it with your hands.

front.en: Maitland Joint Mobilization: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Maitland Joint Mobilization: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Unstable fracture, dislocation, active infection, or suspected cancer in the area. • Worsening neurological signs, or uncertainty about blood vessel safety (especially in the neck). • Take extra care in hypermobile joints, recent trauma and highly irritable pain.
back.ur: Unstable fracture, dislocation, active infection, or suspected cancer in the area. • Worsening neurological signs, or uncertainty about blood vessel safety (especially in the neck). • Take extra care in hypermobile joints, recent trauma and highly irritable pain.

front.en: Concave tibia moves on a convex femur in knee extension. Which way does the tibia glide?
front.ur: Concave tibia moves on a convex femur in knee extension. Which way does the tibia glide?

back.en: Forward, in the same direction as the shaft moves.
back.ur: Forward, in the same direction as the shaft moves.

front.en: What is Stage I traction for?
front.ur: What is Stage I traction for?

back.en: To relieve pressure and settle pain, with no stretch.
back.ur: To relieve pressure and settle pain, with no stretch.

front.en: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization: what does "Convex / concave" mean?
front.ur: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization: "Convex / concave" ka matlab?

back.en: Convex is rounded outward like a ball; concave is curved inward like a cup.
back.ur: Convex is rounded outward like a ball; concave is curved inward like a cup.

front.en: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization: what does "Treatment plane" mean?
front.ur: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization: "Treatment plane" ka matlab?

back.en: An imaginary flat plane across the concave joint surface. Gliding runs parallel to it and traction runs at right angles to it.
back.ur: An imaginary flat plane across the concave joint surface. Gliding runs parallel to it and traction runs at right angles to it.

front.en: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Unstable joints, acute fractures, active infection or inflammation, and suspected tumour. • Hypermobile joints, where you stabilize instead of stretching. • Any worsening neurological symptoms during the technique.
back.ur: Unstable joints, acute fractures, active infection or inflammation, and suspected tumour. • Hypermobile joints, where you stabilize instead of stretching. • Any worsening neurological symptoms during the technique.

front.en: What does 'distraction' mean?
front.ur: What does 'distraction' mean?

back.en: Pulling joint surfaces directly apart.
back.ur: Pulling joint surfaces directly apart.

front.en: Symptoms spread down the arm during traction. What do you do?
front.ur: Symptoms spread down the arm during traction. What do you do?

back.en: Stop and reassess; do not continue.
back.ur: Stop and reassess; do not continue.

front.en: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction: what does "Distraction" mean?
front.ur: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction: "Distraction" ka matlab?

back.en: Separating two joint surfaces by pulling them directly apart.
back.ur: Separating two joint surfaces by pulling them directly apart.

front.en: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction: what does "Long-axis traction" mean?
front.ur: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction: "Long-axis traction" ka matlab?

back.en: Pulling along the length of the limb, for example pulling the arm away from the shoulder.
back.ur: Pulling along the length of the limb, for example pulling the arm away from the shoulder.

front.en: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Instability, fracture, infection, or rheumatoid involvement of the upper neck. • Symptoms that spread or neurological signs that worsen during traction. • Dizziness, visual change or nausea during cervical traction.
back.ur: Instability, fracture, infection, or rheumatoid involvement of the upper neck. • Symptoms that spread or neurological signs that worsen during traction. • Dizziness, visual change or nausea during cervical traction.

front.en: What does PILL stand for?
front.ur: What does PILL stand for?

back.en: Pain-free, Instant result, Long-lasting.
back.ur: Pain-free, Instant result, Long-lasting.

front.en: No immediate improvement after several tries. What next?
front.ur: No immediate improvement after several tries. What next?

back.en: Change the direction slightly or abandon the technique.
back.ur: Change the direction slightly or abandon the technique.

front.en: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM): what does "PILL response" mean?
front.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM): "PILL response" ka matlab?

back.en: Pain-free, Instant result, Long-lasting. The three signs that an MWM is right.
back.ur: Pain-free, Instant result, Long-lasting. The three signs that an MWM is right.

front.en: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM): what does "Sustained glide" mean?
front.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM): "Sustained glide" ka matlab?

back.en: A held, comfortable joint glide that does not oscillate.
back.ur: A held, comfortable joint glide that does not oscillate.

front.en: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM): when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM): kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: No immediate pain-free improvement after a few careful tries. • Unstable joints, fractures, infection or inflammation, and where glides are unsafe. • Any increase in pain, dizziness or neurological symptoms.
back.ur: No immediate pain-free improvement after a few careful tries. • Unstable joints, fractures, infection or inflammation, and where glides are unsafe. • Any increase in pain, dizziness or neurological symptoms.

front.en: In which direction is the cervical SNAG glide applied?
front.ur: In which direction is the cervical SNAG glide applied?

back.en: Along the facet plane, roughly toward the patient's eyes.
back.ur: Along the facet plane, roughly toward the patient's eyes.

front.en: The patient feels dizzy. What do you do?
front.ur: The patient feels dizzy. What do you do?

back.en: Stop immediately and reassess for safety.
back.ur: Stop immediately and reassess for safety.

front.en: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs: what does "Apophyseal joint" mean?
front.ur: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs: "Apophyseal joint" ka matlab?

back.en: Another name for the facet joint, the small paired joints at the back of each vertebra.
back.ur: Another name for the facet joint, the small paired joints at the back of each vertebra.

front.en: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs: what does "Sustained glide" mean?
front.ur: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs: "Sustained glide" ka matlab?

back.en: A held glide with the patient moving through it.
back.ur: A held glide with the patient moving through it.

front.en: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Dizziness, visual disturbance, difficulty speaking or swallowing, or any neurological sign. • Fracture, instability, infection or unexplained severe pain. • No instant pain-free improvement.
back.ur: Dizziness, visual disturbance, difficulty speaking or swallowing, or any neurological sign. • Fracture, instability, infection or unexplained severe pain. • No instant pain-free improvement.

front.en: What is a PA glide?
front.ur: What is a PA glide?

back.en: Pushing a vertebra from back to front.
back.ur: Pushing a vertebra from back to front.

front.en: Which is more reliable, pain response or perceived stiffness?
front.ur: Which is more reliable, pain response or perceived stiffness?

back.en: Pain response.
back.ur: Pain response.

front.en: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization: what does "PA (posteroanterior) glide" mean?
front.ur: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization: "PA (posteroanterior) glide" ka matlab?

back.en: Pushing a vertebra from back to front.
back.ur: Pushing a vertebra from back to front.

front.en: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization: what does "Central vs unilateral" mean?
front.ur: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization: "Central vs unilateral" ka matlab?

back.en: Central pushes on the spinous process in the midline. Unilateral pushes on one side near the facet.
back.ur: Central pushes on the spinous process in the midline. Unilateral pushes on one side near the facet.

front.en: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Suspected fracture, instability or serious pathology (use medical assessment first). • Severe pain or irritability where testing would cause a flare. • Any neurological deficit that is progressing.
back.ur: Suspected fracture, instability or serious pathology (use medical assessment first). • Severe pain or irritability where testing would cause a flare. • Any neurological deficit that is progressing.

front.en: Does a pop mean the joint was put back in place?
front.ur: Does a pop mean the joint was put back in place?

back.en: No. Judge success by retesting movement and pain.
back.ur: No. Judge success by retesting movement and pain.

front.en: When is neck manipulation not appropriate?
front.ur: When is neck manipulation not appropriate?

back.en: When vascular or upper-cervical risk cannot be excluded, or other red flags are present.
back.ur: When vascular or upper-cervical risk cannot be excluded, or other red flags are present.

front.en: HVLA Thrust Manipulation: what does "Thrust / manipulation" mean?
front.ur: HVLA Thrust Manipulation: "Thrust / manipulation" ka matlab?

back.en: A fast, small-amplitude movement at the end of range.
back.ur: A fast, small-amplitude movement at the end of range.

front.en: HVLA Thrust Manipulation: what does "Cavitation" mean?
front.ur: HVLA Thrust Manipulation: "Cavitation" ka matlab?

back.en: The popping sound, likely from gas changes inside the joint. It is not proof of a good result.
back.ur: The popping sound, likely from gas changes inside the joint. It is not proof of a good result.

front.en: HVLA Thrust Manipulation: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: HVLA Thrust Manipulation: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Fracture, osteoporosis, infection, cancer, spinal instability or inflammatory spine disease. • Neurological deficit, cauda equina signs, anticoagulant use or blood vessel concerns. • Neck manipulation when vascular or upper-cervical risk cannot be excluded. • The patient does not consent, is highly irritable or very apprehensive.
back.ur: Fracture, osteoporosis, infection, cancer, spinal instability or inflammatory spine disease. • Neurological deficit, cauda equina signs, anticoagulant use or blood vessel concerns. • Neck manipulation when vascular or upper-cervical risk cannot be excluded. • The patient does not consent, is highly irritable or very apprehensive.

front.en: Difference between sliders and tensioners?
front.ur: Difference between sliders and tensioners?

back.en: Sliders shorten one end while lengthening the other. Tensioners lengthen both ends.
back.ur: Sliders shorten one end while lengthening the other. Tensioners lengthen both ends.

front.en: What is structural differentiation for?
front.ur: What is structural differentiation for?

back.en: To check whether symptoms change when a distant joint moves, suggesting a neural source.
back.ur: To check whether symptoms change when a distant joint moves, suggesting a neural source.

front.en: Neurodynamic Mobilization: what does "Neural tension test" mean?
front.ur: Neurodynamic Mobilization: "Neural tension test" ka matlab?

back.en: A sequence of limb positions that stresses a nerve, for example the upper limb tension test for the median nerve.
back.ur: A sequence of limb positions that stresses a nerve, for example the upper limb tension test for the median nerve.

front.en: Neurodynamic Mobilization: what does "Slider" mean?
front.ur: Neurodynamic Mobilization: "Slider" ka matlab?

back.en: A movement that slides the nerve without increasing overall tension.
back.ur: A movement that slides the nerve without increasing overall tension.

front.en: Neurodynamic Mobilization: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Neurodynamic Mobilization: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Worsening weakness, spinal cord signs or cauda equina symptoms. • Severe, unstable or rapidly worsening nerve symptoms. • Pushing into sharp pain, lingering numbness or tingling.
back.ur: Worsening weakness, spinal cord signs or cauda equina symptoms. • Severe, unstable or rapidly worsening nerve symptoms. • Pushing into sharp pain, lingering numbness or tingling.

front.en: What is a contract-relax technique?
front.ur: What is a contract-relax technique?

back.en: Stretch to the limit, patient contracts the tight muscle, relaxes, then range is increased.
back.ur: Stretch to the limit, patient contracts the tight muscle, relaxes, then range is increased.

front.en: Why avoid breath-holding?
front.ur: Why avoid breath-holding?

back.en: It can raise blood pressure and reduces relaxation.
back.ur: It can raise blood pressure and reduces relaxation.

front.en: PNF Manual Techniques: what does "D1 / D2 patterns" mean?
front.ur: PNF Manual Techniques: "D1 / D2 patterns" ka matlab?

back.en: Diagonal movement patterns of the arm or leg that combine flexion or extension with rotation.
back.ur: Diagonal movement patterns of the arm or leg that combine flexion or extension with rotation.

front.en: PNF Manual Techniques: what does "Contract-relax" mean?
front.ur: PNF Manual Techniques: "Contract-relax" ka matlab?

back.en: Stretch to the limit, patient contracts the tight muscle, relaxes, then you move to a new range.
back.ur: Stretch to the limit, patient contracts the tight muscle, relaxes, then you move to a new range.

front.en: PNF Manual Techniques: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: PNF Manual Techniques: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Uncontrolled high blood pressure or heart conditions (avoid strong breath-holding). • Acute muscle tear, unstable fracture or joint instability. • Pain that increases during the contraction.
back.ur: Uncontrolled high blood pressure or heart conditions (avoid strong breath-holding). • Acute muscle tear, unstable fracture or joint instability. • Pain that increases during the contraction.

front.en: Across or along the fibres?
front.ur: Across or along the fibres?

back.en: Across the fibres.
back.ur: Across the fibres.

front.en: Why wait for analgesia?
front.ur: Why wait for analgesia?

back.en: Once the area is less sensitive, deeper pressure is tolerable.
back.ur: Once the area is less sensitive, deeper pressure is tolerable.

front.en: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction: what does "Transverse" mean?
front.ur: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction: "Transverse" ka matlab?

back.en: Across the fibres, at right angles to them.
back.ur: Across the fibres, at right angles to them.

front.en: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction: what does "Tendinopathy" mean?
front.ur: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction: "Tendinopathy" ka matlab?

back.en: A painful, overloaded tendon, not always inflamed.
back.ur: A painful, overloaded tendon, not always inflamed.

front.en: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Open wounds, infection, skin problems or bruising. • Calcified or unstable tissue, or any suspected partial or full tear that needs medical review. • Pain that increases sharply or does not settle after the session.
back.ur: Open wounds, infection, skin problems or bruising. • Calcified or unstable tissue, or any suspected partial or full tear that needs medical review. • Pain that increases sharply or does not settle after the session.

front.en: How hard should the contraction be?
front.ur: How hard should the contraction be?

back.en: Gentle, about 20 percent of maximum effort.
back.ur: Gentle, about 20 percent of maximum effort.

front.en: What does RI use?
front.ur: What does RI use?

back.en: The opposite muscle to help the tight muscle relax.
back.ur: The opposite muscle to help the tight muscle relax.

front.en: Muscle Energy Technique (MET): what does "Barrier" mean?
front.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET): "Barrier" ka matlab?

back.en: The point where movement first meets resistance.
back.ur: The point where movement first meets resistance.

front.en: Muscle Energy Technique (MET): what does "Isometric" mean?
front.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET): "Isometric" ka matlab?

back.en: A contraction without joint movement.
back.ur: A contraction without joint movement.

front.en: Muscle Energy Technique (MET): when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET): kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Fracture, acute tear, severe osteoporosis or instability. • Uncontrolled blood pressure problems (avoid breath-holding). • Pain that increases with the contraction.
back.ur: Fracture, acute tear, severe osteoporosis or instability. • Uncontrolled blood pressure problems (avoid breath-holding). • Pain that increases with the contraction.

front.en: Which way do you move the tissue?
front.ur: Which way do you move the tissue?

back.en: Toward comfort, shortening it.
back.ur: Toward comfort, shortening it.

front.en: Typical hold time?
front.ur: Typical hold time?

back.en: About 90 seconds.
back.ur: About 90 seconds.

front.en: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release: what does "Tender point" mean?
front.ur: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release: "Tender point" ka matlab?

back.en: A small, sore spot found by gentle pressure, used as a monitor for positioning.
back.ur: A small, sore spot found by gentle pressure, used as a monitor for positioning.

front.en: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release: what does "Position of comfort" mean?
front.ur: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release: "Position of comfort" ka matlab?

back.en: The position where the tender point hurts least.
back.ur: The position where the tender point hurts least.

front.en: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release: when should you NOT use it?
front.ur: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release: kab NAHI karni chahiye?

back.en: Unstable fracture or serious joint or spine instability. • Positioning causes pain, dizziness or neurological symptoms. • Cannot achieve a comfortable position.
back.ur: Unstable fracture or serious joint or spine instability. • Positioning causes pain, dizziness or neurological symptoms. • Cannot achieve a comfortable position.

front.en: What do you find first?
front.ur: What do you find first?

back.en: The neutral position.
back.ur: The neutral position.

front.en: Typical hold time?
front.ur: Typical hold time?

back.en: About 3 seconds.
back.ur: About 3 seconds.

front.en: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR): what does "Neutral" mean?
